meta.note: Public-reference facts for a decision-support chatbot. plausibility-checked; not a substitute for dam-authority data.

dams.name: Tehri Dam
highlights: Tallest dam in India (260.5 m) and among the tallest in the world.
Full Reservoir Level EL 830 m; spillway system sized for a 15,540 cumec probable maximum flood.
1,000 MW underground powerhouse plus ~1,000 MW variable-speed pumped storage; Koteshwar Dam downstream forms the lower reservoir.
Built in a narrow S-shaped Himalayan gorge with steep abutments; sits in a high seismic zone, so it carries extensive seismic instrumentation.
Helped moderate floods in the upper Ganga in 2010, 2011 and 2013.

dams.name: Bhakra Dam
highlights: One of the highest concrete gravity dams in the world (226 m); a symbol of post-independence nation-building.
Creates the Gobind Sagar reservoir (~168 sq km, ~90 km long), India's third-largest by storage.
Irrigates large parts of Punjab, Haryana and Rajasthan; anchor of the Green Revolution belt.
Powerhouse ~1,325 MW (left + right bank units).

dams.name: Sardar Sarovar Dam
highlights: Terminal dam of the Narmada system; full height 163 m with FRL 138.68 m.
Spillway discharging capacity ~84,949 cumec — among the highest in the world.
Narmada Main Canal (~532 km) is among the world's largest irrigation canals.
Supplies drinking water across Gujarat and Rajasthan besides ~1,450 MW of power.

dams.name: Hirakud Dam
dams.type: composite earth-fill + concrete (one of the longest earthen dams in the world)
highlights: Total length ~25.8 km including dykes — the longest dam in India.
Built specifically to tame Mahanadi delta floods; 64 sluices + 34 crest gates.
Hirakud reservoir declared a Ramsar wetland site (2021).
Two powerhouses (Burla + Chiplima) totalling ~347 MW.

dams.name: Koyna Dam
highlights: Second-largest completed hydroelectric complex in India (~1,960 MW across 4 stages).
Creates the ~50 km long Shivasagar lake in the Western Ghats.
Called the lifeline of Maharashtra for power; key monsoon flood-moderation role.
Region is seismically active (1967 Koynanagar earthquake) — closely instrumented.

dams.name: Idukki Dam
highlights: One of Asia's highest arch dams (169 m), built between two hills (Kuravan/Kurathi).
Underground Moolamattom powerhouse (~780 MW) — Kerala's largest hydro station.
Part of a three-dam system with Cheruthoni and Kulamavu.

dams.name: Nagarjuna Sagar Dam
dams.type: masonry gravity (once the world's largest masonry dam)
highlights: Masonry section ~1.45 km with 26 radial crest gates; total project length ~4.9 km.
FRL +179.8 m with ~312 TMC live storage; irrigates both Telugu states.
Among the earliest giant multipurpose projects of independent India (1956–1967).

dams.name: Srisailam Dam
highlights: ~1,670 MW underground powerhouse — a major peaking station for the southern grid.
Key Krishna-basin regulator between Nagarjuna Sagar upstream and downstream barrages.
Sits in the Nallamala forest/Srisailam tiger reserve landscape.

dams.name: Mettur Dam
highlights: Stanley Reservoir (~93 TMC design, reduced by siltation) — lifeline of the Cauvery delta.
Nearly a century old (1934); a reference case for ageing-masonry surveillance.
~240 MW Stanley powerhouse plus canal powerhouses.

dams.name: Pong Dam
highlights: Tallest earth-fill dam in India (133 m) on the Beas.
Pong reservoir is a Ramsar wetland and major migratory-bird habitat.
~396 MW powerhouse; Beas-link regulator for Indus-system flows.

dams.name: Nathpa Jhakri Dam
highlights: India's largest run-of-river hydro station (~1,500 MW) with a ~27 km headrace tunnel.
Desilting chambers handle Sutlej's heavy Himalayan silt load.
High-head Himalayan scheme — sediment and surge management dominate operations.

dams.name: Tungabhadra Dam
highlights: Early joint Karnataka–Andhra Pradesh project (1953) on a Krishna tributary.
Noted siltation case study — live storage well below design.
Canal network irrigates the Raichur–Ballari belt.

context.dam_safety_act: India's Dam Safety Act (2021) mandates surveillance, O&M manuals, emergency action plans and periodic safety reviews for specified dams, enforced via the National Dam Safety Authority (NDSA) and State Dam Safety Organisations (SDSOs).
context.eap_note: Every large dam is required to maintain an Emergency Action Plan with inundation maps, notification flowcharts and response levels.
